ventures.notes: Two listed classes that share equally in dividends: non-voting Class A (FOXA) and voting Class B (FOX), both on the Nasdaq Global Select Market; no preferred or series common stock is outstanding. Class A is the 10-Q cover count plus the approximately 144.5 million Class A shares the November 6, 2026 Form 8-K says FOX will issue to former Roku stockholders. That sum is approximate. It excludes shares issuable for Roku equity awards and Dissenting Shares, and no filing yet states the post-closing total. Class B is unchanged by the merger. The stake is LGC Holdco's: 19,000 Class A shares (under 1%) and 85,372,810 Class B shares (38.76% of the voting class). Its Class B figure is as of the June 16, 2026 Schedule 13D/A, as the proxy footnote says. pctVoting is that Class B percentage, since Class A votes only in limited circumstances. The proxy gives no economic percentage, so pctEconomic is null. In September 2025, as part of the resolution of the Murdoch Family Trust litigation, LGC Holdco acquired additional shares from departing trust beneficiaries. LGC Holdco is managed by Cruden 2, LLC, whose managing director, appointed by Lachlan Murdoch, decides how its shares are voted and sold. Lachlan Murdoch disclaims beneficial ownership. 37,002,060 of its Class B shares are pledged. The proxy does not list Rupert Murdoch, who has been Chairman Emeritus since November 2023, as a holder.

notes: News Corp, the primary company, stays in research/lenses/marketcap. The 2023 press release (filed by Fox as Exhibit 99.1) calls Fox and News Corp the companies Rupert Murdoch founded. Fox Corporation itself was incorporated in Delaware in 2018. It became a standalone public company on March 19, 2019, when Twenty-First Century Fox, Inc. (21CF) spun it off to 21CF stockholders (FY2026 Form 10-K, Item 1), so `founded.year` is the incorporation year of the current company. Murdoch ran its predecessor 21CF as Chief Executive Officer from 1979 to 2015 (2023 proxy statement).
